history.aek: AEK Athens was established in 1924 by Greek refugees from Constantinople in the wake of the Greco-Turkish War. Operating out of Nea Filadelfeia, Athens, the club symbolizes the athletic and cultural heritage of the Greek diaspora.
history.panathinaikos: Founded in 1908 in central Athens, Panathinaikos is the oldest active football club in Greece. Its historic Apostolos Nikolaidis stadium in Ambelokipi has been the heart of Athenian sports for over a century.
history.olympiacos: Formed in 1925 in the bustling port city of Piraeus, Olympiacos originally represented the working class and seafaring community. They are historically the most successful club in Greek football.
history.paok: Originating in 1926 from Greek refugees from Constantinople settling in Thessaloniki, PAOK is the athletic pride of Northern Greece. Their Toumba Stadium is famous for its passionate, intense atmosphere.
history.aris: Aris was founded in 1914 in Thessaloniki, named after Ares, the ancient Greek God of War. Historically representing the urban youth and progressive elements of Macedonia, it is one of Greece's oldest football pillars.
history.panetolikos: Located in Agrinio, Aetolia-Acarnania, Panetolikos was established in 1930 with a strong educational and social philosophy. It is considered the most prominent club of Western Greece.
history.asteras_tripolis: Founded in 1931 in Tripoli, Arcadia, Asteras represents the central Peloponnese region. In the 21st century, the club surged from regional leagues to become a consistent European contender.
history.atromitos: Atromitos was established in 1923 and is based in Peristeri, the largest municipality in western Athens. It carries a strong, working-class, local suburban identity.
history.volos: A modern club founded in 2017 in the coastal city of Volos, Thessaly. Volos NPS rapidly ascended to the Super League, representing the major port city of Central Greece in top-flight football.
history.ofi: OFI Crete was founded in 1925 in Heraklion. It stands as the historic flagship club of the island of Crete, characterized by a fierce, proud, and fiercely loyal local fan base.
history.panserraikos: Founded in 1964 from a merger of local Serres teams, Panserraikos represents the Serres region in Central Macedonia. The club is known as the 'Lions', a nod to the Lion of Amphipolis.
history.ael: Athlitiki Enosi Larisas (AEL) was formed in 1964 in the agricultural heartland of Thessaly. They are the only team outside of the 'Big Two' cities (Athens/Thessaloniki) to have won the Greek Championship (1988).
history.levadiakos: Based in Levadia, Central Greece, Levadiakos was formed in 1961. The club is a sporting anchor for the Boeotia region, frequently bouncing between the first and second national tiers.
history.kifisia: Founded in 2012 in the affluent northern suburbs of Athens, Kifisia FC is a rapidly rising modern club that recently achieved their first-ever historic promotion to the Greek Super League.
history.kavala: One of the most historic clubs in Eastern Macedonia, Kavala FC was founded in 1965.
history.iraklis: One of the oldest and most historic athletic clubs in Greece, founded in 1908 in Thessaloniki.
history.panionios: A historic pillar of Greek football established in 1890, representing the roots of Smyrna and Nea Smyrni.
history.pas_giannina: The prides of Epirus, known as the 'Ajax of Epirus'. Founded in 1966.
history.kalamata: Known as the 'Black Storm', Kalamata represents the Messenia region of the Peloponnese.
history.niki_volou: A historic refugee club formed in 1924, representing the working-class roots of Volos.
history.chania: A rising force representing the majestic city of Chania, Crete.
history.egaleo: The 'City' club from the western suburbs of Athens, with a rich first division history.
history.anagennisi_karditsas: The historic athletic emblem of the Karditsa region in Thessaly.
history.makedonikos: A historic multi-sport club based in Neapoli, Thessaloniki.
history.kallithea: Athens Kallithea FC is rapidly rising as a modern cosmopolitan club from southern Athens.
history.kampaniakos: Representing the region of Chalastra in Central Macedonia.
history.ilioupoli: The central sporting entity of the Ilioupoli municipality in Athens.
history.panargiakos: A historic club representing the ancient city of Argos in the Peloponnese.
history.ellas_syrou: One of the oldest clubs in the Cyclades, representing the island of Syros.
history.nestos: Representing Chrysoupoli, Kavala, Nestos is a traditional force in local football.
history.marko: Representing Markopoulo in East Attica, established in 1927.
history.paok_b: The reserve development team of PAOK FC, competing to forge the next generation of northern talent.
history.olympiacos_b: The youth development squad of Olympiacos FC, grooming future red-and-white stars.
history.asteras_b: The developmental B-squad for Asteras Tripolis, offering crucial experience for academy graduates.
history.gamma_56: MGS Orestis Orestiadas is a historic Greek sports club based in Orestiada, in the Evros regional unit, founded in 1927 through the merger of local clubs "Atlas" and "Ermis". Sporting light blue and white colors, the team has historically achieved notable success, including appearances in the second and third tiers of Greek football, while also winning numerous local championships and Evros Cups over its long history.
history.gamma_57: NPS Veria 1960 represents the continuation of GAS Veria (founded in 1960 through the merger of PAO Vermion and AO Ermis) and is the city's most historic football club, widely known by its nickname, "the 'Queen of the North". Sporting its traditional crimson and blue colors and playing at the Veria Municipal Stadium, the team officially adopted its current name (formerly NPS Veria 2019) following a court ruling in 2024, continuing its journey starting from the local divisions.
history.gamma_58: OFPF Ethnikos is one of the oldest and most historic Greek football and multi-sports clubs, based in Piraeus and officially founded in 1923. The football department, sporting traditional blue and white colors, boasts 36 appearances in the Greek top tier (including 30 consecutive seasons from 1959 to 1990) and historically stands out for winning the second-ever Greek Cup during the 1932–33 season.
history.gamma_59: PAE Akrites Sykeon is a historic football club based in Sykies, Thessaloniki, officially founded in 1939 and recognized by its blue and white colors. The club reached its peak in the 1970s when it competed in the Greek second division (1975-76), and recently, after winning the Macedonia Football Clubs Association (EPSM) championship in 2025, it secured promotion to the Gamma Ethniki following a 32-year absence from the national divisions.
history.gamma_60: PAO Doxa Vyronos is a historic Greek football club based in Vyronas, Athens, officially founded in 1945. Sporting blue and white colors, the team has a history of competing in the second and third tiers of Greek football and recently celebrated its promotion back to the Gamma Ethniki in 2025, following an 11-year absence.
history.gamma_61: PAO Kentavros Vrilission is an amateur football club based in Vrilissia, Athens, established in 2003 by a group of 29 people aiming to create a model academy and a healthy sporting environment for local youth. The club achieved its most historic milestone during the 2024–25 season by winning the Group 1 championship of the Athens Football Clubs Association (EPSA) First Division for the first time, thereby securing promotion to the Gamma Ethniki (the Greek third tier).
history.gamma_62: PAOK Dytikou is an amateur football club based in Dytiko, a small village in the Pella regional unit of Greece. The team achieved a historic milestone for its local community by winning the Pella Football Clubs Association (EPS Pella) championship, which earned them promotion to the Gamma Ethniki (the Greek third tier) for the first time in their history.
history.gamma_63: PAOK Kristonis is an amateur football club based in Kristoni, in the Kilkis regional unit, competing in the Greek national divisions and recognized as one of the most competitive teams in its region. The team has won multiple championships in the Kilkis Football Clubs Association (EPS Kilkis), competed in both the Delta and Gamma Ethniki tiers, and notably reached the third round of the Greek Cup in 2022.
history.gamma_64: PAS Korinthos is a historic Greek football club based in the city of Korinthos. Originally founded in 1963 as APS Korinthos (through the merger of Pankorinthiakos and Aris Korinthou), it adopted its current name in 1999 following a new merger. Sporting red, yellow, and black colors, the team plays its home matches at the Corinth Municipal Stadium and has historically spent several seasons competing in the Greek top tier.
history.gamma_65: PAS Lamia 1964 is a Greek professional football club based in Lamia, officially founded on June 1, 1964, following the merger of local clubs Pamfthiotikos, Olympiakos Lamias, and Pallamiaki. Sporting blue and white colors and playing its home matches at the Lamia Municipal Sports Center, the team has established itself as a steady presence in the professional tiers of Greek football in recent years.
history.gamma_66: PAS Pyrgos 1968 is a Greek football club based in Pyrgos (Ilia), formed in 2025 when AO Thyella Katarrachiou Pyrgou (originally founded in 1968) absorbed the historic club Paniliakos. Sporting the red and white colors and the torch emblem of Paniliakos, the team plays its home matches at the Municipal Stadium of Pyrgos and competes in the Gamma Ethniki, while also maintaining a women's football team.
history.gamma_67: PO Atsaleniou (POA) is a historic Greek sports club based in Atsalenio, a suburb of Heraklion, Crete, founded in 1951 by Asia Minor refugees. Considered one of the most dynamic clubs in Heraklion, the team plays its home matches at the privately owned Atsalenios Stadium, established in 1960, and has predominantly competed in the Gamma Ethniki and Delta Ethniki divisions.
history.gamma_68: PO Elassonas is a historic football club from Elassona in the Larisa region, originally founded in 1922 as Proodeftikos Omilos before being re-established under its current name in 1957. Playing its home matches at the Elassona Municipal Stadium, the team has historically competed as high as the Greek second tier and, after a brief merger with local rival AO Olosson in 2007, reverted to its traditional name and identity in 2011.
history.gamma_69: Proodos Rogon 1966 is an amateur football club based in Nea Kerasounta (Arta) and playing its home matches at the Nea Kerasounta ground. Despite the “1966” in its name, it got founded just at 2023
history.gamma_70: PS Ethnikos Neo Keramidi is a Greek professional football club founded in 1951 and based in the small village of Neo Keramidi, near Katerini in the Pieria region. The team achieved the greatest milestone in its history during the 2023-2024 season by winning their Gamma Ethniki group and earning promotion to the professional Super League 2 for the very first time.
history.gamma_71: SFK Pierikos is a historic Greek football club based in Katerini, founded on April 11, 1961, following the merger of local clubs Megas Alexandros and Olympos Katerinis. It is the most successful club in the Pieria regional unit, having spent many seasons in the Greek top tier and reaching the Greek Cup final in 1963, where they played against Olympiacos.
history.gamma_72: FS Eordaikos Ptolemaida is a historic football club from Western Macedonia, Greece, founded in 1978 through the merger of local teams Aris and Ptolemaios. Based in the city of Ptolemaida, the team sports green and yellow colors and has historically competed in the second and third tiers of Greek football.
history.gamma_73: FS Kozani is a Greek football club founded in 1964 following the merger of local teams Makedonikos and Olympiakos Kozanis. Based in the city of Kozani, the team plays its home matches at the Municipal Stadium of Kozani and sports red and white as its official colors.
